l.i: Horribilis & terribilis est (Chaldaeorū gens:) ex seipsa iudicium eius & dignitas eius egredietur. Leniores sunt Pardis equi eius, & acutiores lupis uespertinis: quam-plurimi sunt equites eius qui de longè ue-nient, & aduolabunt tanquam aquila fe-stinans ad comedendum.

main_text.l: Pergit Dominus in descriptione exer-citus Chaldaeorum, ac hæcilli tribuit:

1. Quòd sit horribilis ac terribilis: ut ingenium crudelissimæ gentis, & belli effectum indicet, de quo Pindarus rectè pronunciauit: γλυκὺ δὲ πόλεμος ἀπείροισιν· ἐμπείρων δὲ [?]ς ταχέα [?] προσιόντα νιν [?] λαχρδίας [?] πει- ραστῶς [?].
2. Quòd pro suo arbitrio de iure respo-deat, leges figat & refigat, euehat in altū & deijciat quos uisum est. Hoc enim existimo sibi uelle illam phrasin, Ex seipsa iudicium eius,&c.

3. Quòd eius equestres copiæ, celerita-te Pardos & aquilas: rapacitate lupos uè spertinos, qui tota die fame laborauerunt, & uespere prodeunt uenatum, ut medeantur fami, referant. Addita est autem am-plifi-

page.notes: Greek quotation in item 1 (Pindar) is doubtful in several words, marked [?]; the second line and the final word are the least certain. "luposuè" in item 3 is run together in print and may be "lupos ue". Long s is printed as a f-like form throughout and is transcribed as s. Hyphenated line-end words kept with printed hyphens. Left margin notes read "Lectio 11." and "11. Septembr." Page ends mid-word ("amplifi-"), continuing on the next page.
